Right now

Making LetsGo Ride work beyond the pitch deck.

The interesting part is not drawing another ride-booking screen. It is deciding what a driver in Zimbabwe needs to trust, what a passenger needs to understand in five seconds, and which assumptions from bigger markets simply do not travel.

I’m building through those questions one release at a time.

The work

No pretend case-study metrics. Just what each product is, what makes it difficult, and the decision I am making next.

Mobility / ZimbabweLive product

LetsGo Ride

A ride platform built for the way people actually move in Zimbabwe.

The decision

Keep the flow direct. Make the important actions obvious. Remove anything that slows a rider or driver down.

Things I’m still figuring out

How do you build trust before you have scale?

  • What changes when a product is designed from Zimbabwe outward?
  • How much should software explain, and how much should it simply get out of the way?
  • When does restraint become hesitation?
A useful constraint

I refuse to build something just because the demo looks good.

If the product cannot survive slow networks, awkward edge cases, a busy front desk or a driver using it between trips, the polished mock-up means very little.
